claims.text: High-entropy alloys can combine high strength with excellent ductility through synergistic activation of deformation twinning and dislocation slip.
In CoCrFeNi nanopillars, deformation twinning and dislocation slip are spatially and synergistically coordinated.
Atomic-scale chemical compositional heterogeneities initiate the joint or sequential activation of twinning and dislocation slip.
Local chemical heterogeneities generate a wide distribution of generalized stacking-fault energies.
Regions with lower local stacking-fault energies preferentially activate deformation twinning.
Regions with higher local stacking-fault energies preferentially favor dislocation glide.
Spatially coordinated twinning and dislocation slip delocalize deformation.
Spatially coordinated twinning and dislocation slip enhance work hardening.
Spatially coordinated twinning and dislocation slip delay necking failure and thereby preserve tensile ductility.
An as-processed equiatomic CoCrFeNi alloy inherently contains atomic-scale compositional heterogeneities.
A homogenizing treatment or minor micro-alloying addition can reduce atomic-scale compositional fluctuations in CoCrFeNi.
Reducing local compositional fluctuations will narrow the stacking-fault-energy distribution.
Reducing local compositional fluctuations will lower the dynamically activated twin volume fraction relative to the heterogeneous baseline.
Reducing local compositional fluctuations will reduce the work-hardening rate relative to the baseline.
Reducing local compositional fluctuations will decrease uniform elongation relative to the baseline.
Reducing local compositional fluctuations may slightly increase initial flow stress.
Single-crystalline CoCrFeNi nanopillars can show greater than 100% room-temperature uniform elongation while retaining high flow stress.
The proposed mechanism applies at ambient temperature in single-phase CoCrFeNi-type high-entropy alloys.
The proposed mechanism applies over both micro- and nanoscale specimen dimensions when grain size and other extrinsic variables are controlled.
